title: Behavioral stability and schema adapter policy for pinned model versions
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Objective: Define and implement a practical backward-compatibility policy for pinned model versions that covers behavioral semantics, prompt/schema surface changes, and a lightweight runtime "shim" (schema adapter) to enable graceful evolution without breaking existing customer integrations. Scope includes: (1) formalizing compatibility levels (strict, tolerant, experimental) for prompt and output schemas; (2) publishing a machine-readable performance/profile manifest for each pinned release (latency P99, tokens-per-second baseline, quantization profile); (3) building a schema-adapter library inside the runtime that can normalize incoming prompts and map legacy parameter names to current equivalents; (4) a gated rollout + automated evals to detect semantic drift.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A compatibility-level enum exists in the pinned manifest and is surfaced via the API and Console. 2) Runtime exposes a pluggable schema-adapter interface with two built-in adapters: "strict" (reject mismatched prompts) and "tolerant" (map aliases, fill defaults). 3) Each pinned release includes a performance_profile.json artifact with P50/P95/P99 latencies, baseline throughput, and quantization hints published to the model catalog. 4) Regression harness runs on every pinned release and produces a pass/fail badge; failures require a documented mitigation plan before release. 5) Backwards-compatibility tests and smoke tests are included in CI for dedicated/private deployments.
constraints_and_tradeoffs: - Doing full semantic equivalence checking (model-level behavioral proofs) is out of scope; we rely on eval suites and human-reviewed migration notes. - Schema adapters increase surface area and may hide breaking changes; therefore adapters must be explicit, opt-in per-customer, and logged. - Performance profiling adds release overhead; we will parallelize profiling to a dedicated fleet to avoid delaying rollouts. - For high-throughput customers, 'tolerant' adapters may add ~1-3 ms per request; provide opt-out via route config.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 sprints): define compatibility enum and manifest schema; add manifest generation to onboarding pipeline; add telemetry hooks for adapter usage. Phase 2 (3 sprints): implement schema-adapter interface in runtime, two adapters (strict/tolerant), and an adapter config API. Phase 3 (2 sprints): integrate perf profiling agent into staging, publish performance_profile artifact to model catalog, and add acceptance checks in the release pipeline. Phase 4 (ongoing): monitor field telemetry, add more adapters and expand eval suites.
migration_strategy: - Default for existing pinned versions: mark compatibility level 'strict' to preserve current behavior. - New pinned releases: authors choose compatibility level and attach migration notes. - Customers on Dedicated/Private get an opt-in flag 'allow_adapter' and a per-route adapter config. - Provide a CLI tool to run the release eval locally against customer prompt sets to validate behavior before flipping the adapter.
telemetry_and_alerting: Emit adapter usage metrics (adapter.type, mapped_fields_count, map_latency_ms), semantic-regression alerts (eval_score_drop > threshold), and perf-regression alerts (P99 latency increase > 15%). Add Console dashboard: 'Pinned Compatibility' with per-model compatibility level, adapter adoption, and recent regression runs.
test_plan: - Unit tests for adapter field-mapping and default-filling logic. - Integration tests exercising manifest read/write and adapter pipeline. - Regression harness: run canonical prompt set (1000 examples) and compare n-gram and semantic similarity metrics to baseline. - Load test to quantify added latency for tolerant adapter and effect on batching/kv cache.
rollout_and_fallback: Rollout: feature-flagged in staging -> canary in hosted API -> gradual percentage ramp guided by telemetry. Fallback: runtime can disable adapter per-route and fail open to previous pinned behavior; automated rollback if semantic-regression or perf-regression thresholds exceeded.
open_questions: What is the canonical shape for performance_profile.json? (see PR #42)
Do we allow adapters to rewrite tokens or only map parameter names and fill missing fields?
Should we offer an official 'compatibility shim' client SDK or rely on server-side adapters?
